items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee (Jimmy Jones) is narrating a story about Eubie Blake and Perry Bradford. The interviewee does not claim a personal relationship with Perry Bradford, but rather describes events involving Eubie Blake and Perry Bradford.

ctx.x: Oh, this is a funny story. It's a very funny story. Well, Perry Bradford -- a lot of people know who Eubie Blake is, but Perry Bradford had written -- he's written some old time songs that have become standards. And -- but he was always a hustler. He was always trying to tell Eubie where to put his money. He says, "This guy's name is Chase." He's talking about the Chase National Bank. He says -- he's talking to Eubie, this is Perry talking to Eubie. He says, "But, Cos, --" he called him Cos -- he said, "Cos,…

doesn't have a nickel in his pocket to get home. And he's sitting there shaking his head. He's a black man, but he turned white as a sheet, because he's got all this money and he can't move, you know. So Eubie gave him I think it was a dollar, maybe a dollar and forty-six, cents, something like that, to get to the Bronx, and this was like in 1920 and 1921, and Perry got home. Oh, he made a whole lot of money since then, but he never paid Eubie back.
